checks.statement: Snackbars may either disappear temporarily on their own (dismissive) or remain until the user takes action (non-dismissive); M3 also uses updated color mappings compatible with dynamic color.
checks.condition: When selecting a snackbar dismissal mode or applying M3 colors.

sourceHistory.summary: M2 comparison describes the two dismissal modes and dynamic-color mapping change.

evidence.result: Actionable bars do not schedule auto-dismissal. Actionless bars require a data-snackbar-inline target before a timer starts; their message is copied there. Dismissal restores focus only when it was inside the bar. F6 focuses an available action and is documented beside the trigger.
Three runtime tests pass for persistent/actionless timing, inline retention, focus restoration and F6 guards. Go checks the associated visible shortcut hint.

Chromium: seven assertions pass, including staying open after the former six-second timeout, focus on open, F6, action dismissal and Escape. Lifetime and F6 failed on their respective pre-fix versions. Real F6 input on the component page focuses Undo.

implementation.notes: The actual page contains an action. The optional actionless/inline composition is unit-tested, not exposed as a separate playground configuration. Screen-reader announcements have not been listened to.

checks.statement: Use snackbars for low-priority process updates that do not require action; people should remain able to browse the page. Show only one snackbar at a time and allow at most one action; dismiss/cancel actions are optional. Use a dialog for high-priority messages that require immediate action or block app use.
checks.condition: When choosing a component and action model for a message.

sourceHistory.summary: Usage guidance specifies snackbar priority, non-interruption, one-at-a-time display, and action limit relative to dialogs.

evidence.result: The specimen provides one action and a dismiss button, but usage frequency, priority threshold and whether a product action is core are application decisions not enforced by the component.

implementation.notes: No application-level priority/frequency integration is included.

sourceHistory.summary: Web accessibility guidance requires a second inline or nearby message channel.

checks.statement: Relate the text label directly to the process performed. Keep it short and clear, one line when possible, and at most two lines at compact breakpoints. Avoid icons, stylized text, and inline links; use a different component for icon- or link-heavy messages, or provide a button for the action.
checks.condition: When writing snackbar message content.

sourceHistory.summary: Text-label guidance defines message relevance and length and cautions against icons, stylized text, and links.

evidence.result: The specimen uses plain text and one/two-line variants, but its two-line content includes an explicit line break and no responsive compact wrapping rule is evidenced.

implementation.notes: Copy quality and compact rendered line count require product/content and viewport review.

checks.statement: Use a completely opaque rectangular gray container by default so the text remains legible; slight transparency is allowed only while text stays clearly legible. Avoid significantly changing the container shape. Keep the text label and action text visually distinct, and do not use filled or elevated action buttons.
checks.condition: When styling the snackbar container and action.

sourceHistory.summary: Container guidance covers opacity, shape, text legibility, label/action contrast, and button emphasis.

evidence.result: Container shape and fill are token-bound and action uses a text-button variant, but opacity and gray-container contrast are not established without resolved token/color inspection.

implementation.notes: Actual opacity and contrast were not measured.

checks.statement: A snackbar may contain one text-button action, but it must not be the only way to access a core use case. Use colored action text to distinguish it from the message; a long action may occupy a third line. An Undo action can let users amend a choice; a Dismiss action is usually unnecessary because snackbars disappear by default.
checks.condition: When a snackbar includes an action.

sourceHistory.summary: Action guidance describes count, distinction, line allowance, undo use, and optional dismissal.

evidence.result: The snackbar includes one Undo text button plus a separate labeled dismiss icon; the action is not the only way to dismiss the snackbar.

checks.statement: Place snackbars at the bottom in front of main content; they may move upward to avoid a FAB or docked toolbar. Do not cover navigation, frequently used touch targets, focused/actionable elements, or FABs; place them above FABs. Full-width snackbars are appropriate only when persistent navigation is absent. A snackbar may push a FAB upward when shown.
checks.condition: When placing a snackbar over page content and other controls.

sourceHistory.summary: Placement guidance covers bottom layering, collision avoidance, focus visibility, full-width constraint, and FAB relation.

evidence.result: The snackbar popover is fixed at the viewport bottom and horizontally centered; no collision-avoidance or adjustment above a FAB, toolbar, navigation, or focused control is implemented.

checks.statement: At compact breakpoints, expand snackbar height from 48dp to 64dp for one or two lines while keeping fixed distances from the screen's leading, trailing, and bottom edges.
checks.condition: At compact window breakpoints.

sourceHistory.summary: Compact layout guidance specifies height range and fixed edge spacing.

evidence.result: The container has a token-backed fixed minimum height and no compact breakpoint rule that expands it to 64dp or sets leading/trailing/bottom viewport margins.

checks.statement: At medium and expanded breakpoints, scale the snackbar horizontally for longer messages and aim for a 40–60 character line length, ideally one line with an optional button. Use flexible trailing-edge spacing. Left or center alignment is allowed if placement stays consistent; do not place it flush to a layout edge or show consecutive snackbars side by side.
checks.condition: At medium and expanded window breakpoints.

sourceHistory.summary: Large-layout guidance covers width, line length, optional action, alignment, and edge/adjacency limits.

evidence.result: The snackbar uses max-content width with no medium/expanded breakpoint sizing or target line length; its text is explicitly nowrap.

checks.statement: Show snackbars without blocking page interaction. Snackbars without actions may dismiss after 4–10 seconds depending on platform; avoid auto-dismiss on web unless inline feedback is also present. Keep snackbars with actions visible until the user acts or dismisses them.
checks.condition: When choosing snackbar lifetime and interaction behavior.

sourceHistory.summary: Behavior section specifies non-blocking display and conditional lifetime by action and platform.

checks.statement: Display consecutive snackbars one at a time, never stacked. An updated message may replace an outdated snackbar immediately. Do not animate other components, such as a FAB, along with snackbar animations.
checks.condition: When multiple snackbar messages occur in sequence.

sourceHistory.summary: Consecutive guidance requires sequential display and limits coordinated animations.

evidence.result: A timer is stored per snackbar element and each demo can open its own popover; there is no cross-demo queue/replacement controller.

implementation.notes: Component-local source does not establish whether the host app guarantees a single global snackbar.

checks.statement: Assistive-technology users must be alerted without disruption, be able to move focus to actionable snackbars, and take their actions.
checks.condition: For accessible snackbars.

sourceHistory.summary: Use cases list alerting, focus access, and action tasks.

evidence.result: The visible snackbar exposes status semantics and has focusable action/dismiss buttons with an accessible label for the icon control.

checks.statement: Do not auto-dismiss snackbars that have actions. Actionless snackbars may dismiss after a sufficient platform-specific duration; 4–10 seconds is a common acceptable range. Use the default color mapping so the snackbar stands out without color conflicts.
checks.condition: When selecting snackbar lifetime and color, especially for assistive-technology users.

sourceHistory.summary: Interaction guidance covers action-dependent persistence, duration range, and default color mapping.

checks.statement: Tab moves focus between interactive snackbar elements; Esc dismisses a snackbar while it is focused.
checks.condition: When keyboard-operating a snackbar.

sourceHistory.summary: Keyboard table maps Tab and Esc behavior.

evidence.result: Action and close controls are native buttons in tab order; Escape hides any open snackbar.

checks.statement: Announce snackbars once when they appear without taking focus. Use a polite live region on Android and web; iOS 17 and later announce politely by default. If a snackbar appears at app launch, announce it after the page title without focusing it.
checks.condition: When announcing a snackbar to screen readers.

sourceHistory.summary: Labeling guidance specifies announcement timing, polite platform behavior, and launch ordering.

evidence.result: The snackbar has role=status and the demo contains an aria-live=polite output; the popover is not focused on open.

checks.statement: Support single-line, single-line with action, two-line, two-line with action, and two-line with a longer action configurations.
checks.condition: When arranging snackbar message and action content.

sourceHistory.summary: Configuration diagram labels five line-count and action combinations.

evidence.result: The specimen branches between one-line and two-line content and always includes an action, but no long-action configuration or responsive line behavior is exercised.

implementation.notes: Only a subset of the listed combinations is represented by the specimen.
